rounds.what_returned: Confirmed real event: F-15E shot down April 3 2026 over western Iran; both crew rescued; A-10 also damaged during rescue. Multiple mainstream sources (NBC, CNN, Al Jazeera, Military Times, TWZ, Wikipedia).
rounds.lesson: Event is real and well-documented. Now need to verify specific factual claims in the tweet's AI-generated video narrative: Mach 2.8 speed, missile types (TOR-M1, Chinese MANPADS), A-10 crash location (tweet says Strait of Hormuz).

rounds.what_returned: A-10 crashed near Strait of Hormuz (Military Times, Newsweek, Aviationist confirm). Trump stated F-15E hit by MANPADS (shoulder-fired), not a TOR-M1 SAM. F-15E maximum speed is ~Mach 2.5, not 2.8 — Mach 2.8 claim is false per multiple sources including Warrior Maven. Specific weapon systems (TOR-M1, Chinese MANPADS, Soviet Su-23 gun) NOT officially confirmed — AI-fabricated details.
rounds.lesson: The Mach 2.8 speed claim is clearly wrong (F-15E tops out at ~Mach 2.5). The specific missile system details (TOR-M1, Chinese shoulder missiles, Soviet Su-23 AA gun) are unverified fabrications presented as fact. Trump confirmed only that a shoulder-fired missile (MANPADS) was used.

queries: McDonnell Douglas F-15E Strike Eagle maximum speed Wikipedia
rounds.what_returned: Wikipedia F-15E article confirmed two-seat crew configuration and other specs, but speed spec not prominently listed. Warrior Maven and others consistently cite Mach 2.5 as max speed.
rounds.lesson: For aircraft specs, dedicated aviation sources (TWZ, Warrior Maven, Air and Space Forces) are more useful than Wikipedia for performance numbers.

insights.would_multipass_help: yes — a second pass specifically targeting the unconfirmed weapon systems (TOR-M1, Chinese MANPADS, Soviet Su-23) with queries like 'Iran F-15E missile type confirmed TOR-M1 false' would strengthen the finding that these are AI fabrications
insights.deepseek_advice: For tweets presenting AI-generated video content as factual reporting on a real military event, first verify the event exists, then target specific technical claims (aircraft speeds, weapon system names, crash locations) against authoritative defense sources — aviation specs are easy to fact-check and AI often confuses numbers like Mach 2.5 vs 2.8. Use 'what missile shot down [aircraft]' + 'official confirmed' to surface whether claimed weapon system details are verified or fabricated.
